clue.text: Seaman, one at home on the water

definitions.meaning: Sir Francis ..., the Elizabethan sea captain and circumnavigator

definitions.text: one at home on the water
definitions.meaning: a male duck, a bird that lives on ponds and rivers

explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was a famous English sailor, and the male of the duck is called by the same name.

clue.text: Rest after match, competitive game

indicators.note: after places the word for rest behind the word for match in the answer

parts.note: a duplicate matches the original exactly
in snooker a bridge is the rest used to support the cue

explanation.surface: A tired player takes a break once the match is over and then plays a competitive game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rest after match' reads as a breather following a fixture; the rest is the snooker cue support, and 'after' puts it second.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of the card game has every table play the same deals, so pairs compete directly on identical hands.

clue.text: Unpleasantly bitter drug — that's about right

indicators.note: about means the drug word goes around the letter for right

parts.note: acid is slang for the hallucinogen LSD

explanation.surface: Someone tasting a nasty medicine grimaces and agrees it is properly bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ACID around R.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, sharp taste or smell that stings is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Ruler has got eastern electoral system into confusion

indicators.note: into means the voting system's letters are put inside the word for confusion

parts.note: a mess is a state of confusion
PR stands for proportional representation, a voting system

explanation.surface: A ruler finds that adopting a foreign voting system has thrown everything into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals that the voting-system letters go inside the word for confusion, with the eastern letter in front. 'Ruler' is the definition at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A female monarch heading an empire is a sovereign who rules.

clue.text: Pot made by Spanish girl broken by Spanish boy

indicators.note: broken by means the girl's name is split open with the boy's name inserted

parts.note: Maria is a common Spanish girl's name
Juan is a common Spanish boy's name

explanation.surface: A cooking pot was made by a Spanish girl and then smashed by a Spanish boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' signals that the girl's name is split by the boy's name. 'Pot' is slang for cannabis, not a cooking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for cannabis, the drug also known by this Spanish-derived name.

clue.text: Food for horses in wood beneath motorway

indicators.note: beneath in a down clue means the tree's letters are placed below the motorway letter

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: Horse feed is found in a wood lying below the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'beneath' puts ASH below M.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran or grain mixed with warm water into a soft feed is given to horses as a mash.

clue.text: A training exercise for soldiers a month after utter defeat by English

indicators.note: after places the month behind the other pieces

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat
March is a month of the year

explanation.surface: Soldiers do a training exercise a month after being thrashed by the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' signals that the month comes last; 'by' only means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: A long march in step-free order over roads, done by troops for fitness and discipline.

clue.text: Stick spies over on a Caribbean island

parts.note: to jam is to stick fast

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the agency's letters are turned upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

explanation.surface: Agents are glued to their posts on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns CIA into AIC; 'on' is a link and 'a' gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large island nation in the West Indies, south of Cuba.

clue.text: Member blowing hard, a trumpet player

parts.note: an arm is a member, or limb, of the body
a strong wind is one blowing hard

explanation.surface: A trumpeter puffs hard into his instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is Louis Armstrong, the American jazz trumpeter.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Armstrong was a celebrated New Orleans jazz trumpeter and singer.

clue.text: What Sinatra had is novel

definitions.meaning: Frank Sinatra was nicknamed Ol' Blue Eyes
an early book by Thomas Hardy, published in 1873

explanation.surface: A fan says the singer's famous feature is also the title of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinatra's nickname came from his striking eye colour, and Thomas Hardy wrote a novel with this title.

clue.text: Together, rum pair get through university

indicators.note: rum means odd or strange, so the letters of the word are mixed up

parts.note: to pass an exam is to get through it

explanation.surface: A pair of tipsy students drink rum together while scraping through their degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like a drink but is the anagram signal: PAIR becomes PARI.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means side by side, on an equal footing, at the same rate.

clue.text: Deadly creature, black, trapped by mother

indicators.note: trapped by means the black letter is held inside the word for mother

parts.note: mama is a word for mother
B is the pencil abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A mother traps a dangerous black animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped by' puts B inside MAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous African snake whose bite can kill quickly.

clue.text: Popular performance for sure

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a deed is something performed, an act

explanation.surface: A crowd-pleasing show, without doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb of emphasis meaning certainly or truly.

clue.text: An honest broker to admire, in conflict

indicators.note: in conflict means the letters are at odds and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A neutral go-between is torn between respect and disagreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in conflict' rearranges TO ADMIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutral third party who settles a dispute between two sides is an honest broker.

clue.text: Promise action

definitions.meaning: a battle or fight between armies

explanation.definitionFit: A betrothal is a promise to wed, and a military clash is also a fight in this sense.

clue.text: Country once hell in one area

parts.note: the abyss is the bottomless pit, hell
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Somewhere in a region of a former country was a place of torment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here: it gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The former name of Ethiopia, used until the twentieth century.

clue.text: In county Kerry, his ring tour

indicators.note: a tour goes round and round, so the letters are turned about

parts.note: a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: A man named Kerry takes his ring on a trip around an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tour' rearranges KERRY, HIS and O. 'Kerry' looks like the Irish county but is fodder; the county is English.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest historic English county, in the north of the country.

clue.text: Detached, a goose flying back

indicators.note: flying back means the word for a silly person is turned to read backwards

parts.note: a goose is a silly person, a fool

explanation.surface: A lone goose flies home, remote from the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying back' turns FOOL into LOOF.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone distant and reserved stands apart from others.

clue.text: Hare off across centre of British ground

indicators.note: across means the rearranged letters stretch around the middle letter
off means the letters have gone wrong, so they are rearranged
centre of picks the middle letter of the word British

explanation.surface: A hare sprints across the middle of a British field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges HARE to EARH; 'centre of' takes T from British, and 'across' puts EARH around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth means soil or the land underfoot.

clue.text: Boxer's second name's king

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name or nickname
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A boxer's corner man is named after a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the boxer's helper in the corner; 'name's' is name has.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is the trainer or helper who manages a boxer during a bout.

clue.text: In fear, change lifestyle here in Russia

indicators.note: In signals that the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone afraid to change their way of life is told to try it in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the letters inside fear, change lifestyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city in northern Russia on the White Sea, now usually Arkhangelsk.

clue.text: Register — girl is able to when trained up

parts.note: Alma is a girl's name

indicators.note: trained up in a down clue means the word is sent upwards and so read backwards

parts.note: can means is able to

explanation.surface: A girl joins a register once she has learnt the job properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained up' turns CAN into NAC; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A yearly book listing dates, tides and other data is a calendar or record of this kind.

clue.text: Took exception to being put on after opener's dismissal

indicators.note: the opener being dismissed means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a play is presented or put on

explanation.surface: A batsman was upset at being sent in after the opening batsman was out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after opener's dismissal' drops the P from PRESENTED. 'Opener' and 'dismissal' borrow cricket words, in which a batsman is dismissed.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel aggrieved at something is to take offence or exception to it.

clue.text: Spike one politician's drink

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone laces a single politician's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' suggests doctoring a drink, but it is the verb to skewer.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something with a sharp point is to spike it.

clue.text: Unproductive female's lost grant

indicators.note: lost means the female letter has gone from the word

parts.note: fallow land is left unplanted, so unproductive

explanation.surface: A barren woman has been refused a grant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes F from FALLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To grant is to permit or concede, so the verb fits.

clue.text: Ordinary iron vessel

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An ordinary iron ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordinary' is a heraldic term: a basic shield charge.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, an ordinary is a simple bold charge; this one is a broad horizontal band across the shield.

clue.text: Train (by repeated practice) a baboon

definitions.meaning: to teach by repetition, as soldiers are on a parade ground
a West African primate related to the mandrill

explanation.surface: A trainer teaches a monkey its routine through repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct by repeated exercises is to drill, and a large West African monkey shares the name.

clue.text: Friend is after novel treen, constantly

indicators.note: after places the word for friend behind the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A pal keeps chasing an unusual set of wooden ware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges TREEN, a word for small wooden items, into ETERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes on forever, without end, happens constantly.

clue.text: Hates bangers being parked by river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
bangers and crates are both slang for old, battered cars

explanation.surface: Someone loathes the old cars left parked by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bangers' look like sausages but are British slang for old cars. The Exe is a river in Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse or loathe intensely is to detest.

clue.text: Crew's leader is indebted to yachting centre

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of the word Crew's

parts.note: to owe is to be indebted

explanation.surface: A ship's captain owes money to a sailing club.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the Isle of Wight town, home of the regatta week.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on the Isle of Wight famous for its annual sailing regatta.
